catalogue_requests.reason: No catalogued class carries an 18-channel detector array without a wavelength axis. cap.measure.spectrum.v1 requires wavelength_min and wavelength_max and returns a wavelength axis, but the clone states no channel wavelengths (README.md:5-9 names only the three LED peaks), so binding it would invent an axis. The extension returns the raw and calibrated arrays in the clone's ascending-frequency order.

No catalogued class expresses a factory reset of this instrument. cap.device.self_test.v1 is a test, not the native init reset, and it does not fit the upstream init() sequence (spectrometer.py:155-160).

No catalogued class expresses a device safe state that turns off the on-board blue and shutter LEDs. cap.imaging.illumination.v1 is a write of an illumination level on a light.source, not a safe-state action on an instrument.spectrometer, and a safe-state action must take no input.

WHY PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED: the card's only entry symbols are the module-level functions spectrometer:init (spectrometer.py:155), spectrometer:readRAW (spectrometer.py:325) and spectrometer:readCAL (spectrometer.py:350); the clone has no class. Gate G7 calls mhs.driver.upstream.class_surface on the native symbol, which parses the clone with Python 3 ast. spectrometer.py is Python 2.7: line 341 is the print statement "print output", so the file cannot be parsed and class_surface reports "spectrometer.py cannot be parsed" for every entry symbol. Because the card's entry_symbols confidence is override, native must equal one of those symbols or G7 reports G7.NOT_AN_ENTRY_SYMBOL; the clone has no parseable class to name instead. The direct and PythonObjectDriver shapes therefore cannot pass G7, and a SerialDriver/ScpiDriver would misstate the I2C register protocol. This is the same Python 2 condition PLAYBOOK.md section 5 records as PLATFORM_UNSUPPORTED (the bernardokyotoku/pydcu package records it the same way). The SDK and the clone were not edited.

The fake defines only public names the upstream module has (readReg, writeReg, setDEVSEL, init, boardPresent, hwVersion, swVersion, temperatures, setBlueLED, shutterLED, setLEDDriveCurrent, setIntegrationTime, setGain, readRAW, readCAL, IEEE754toFloat, reorderData); G7 could not check them because the clone cannot be parsed.

COVERED: reads board_present, hardware_version [type, version], temperatures [three registers], integration_time_register, gain, led_drive_current, blue_led and shutter_leds; configuration writes for those values through cap.device.configure.v1. The integration-time limit is min 0, max 254 with ref spectrometer.py:280 (the code checks range(0,255)); gain and LED drive current use the clone's allowed sets 0..3 (spectrometer.py:303 and :258). cap.measure.intensity.v1 returns one calibrated channel from readCAL, selected by channel "1".."18" in the clone's ascending-frequency order, or the brightest channel when omitted. x-cap.liamsgithub.read_spectrum.v1 returns the 18 raw and 18 calibrated values; x-cap.liamsgithub.factory_reset.v1 calls the native init; x-cap.liamsgithub.leds_off.v1 is the safe-state action and, with the @estop, turns off the blue LED and the three shutter LEDs through setBlueLED(False) and shutterLED(device, False).

NOT COVERED: the wavelength axis of the 18 channels, because the clone states no channel wavelengths (README.md:5-9 names only the three LED peaks at about 400, 475 and 875 nm), so cap.measure.spectrum.v1 is not bound; the Python 2 clone itself is never imported; the hardware backend (native.py, an independent SMBus port) was never run; init() sleeps 4 seconds on hardware, as the clone does (spectrometer.py:158); no physical hardware e-stop is claimed. The array extension carries the full 18 values, not a truncated stand-in.

G4.REF_VALUE: the only warning is expected. The clone's line 280 is "if time not in range(0,255):", so the code accepts 0 through 254 while the docstring at line 274 and README.md:77 say 0 to 255. The driver uses the code's actual maximum 254; the cited line does not literally show 254, and citing 255 would misstate the code. The warning is not suppressed.
